sourceNotes:
# Artwork source comparison

The artwork combines textual references and symbol substitutions. A source match for a phrase does not identify the source of an unknown glyph.

| Element | Source | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small writing forming WELCOME TO THE BRAVE NEW WORLD | Satoshi Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer to Peer Electronic Cash System, section 2, printed page 2 | Confirmed textual match. The title shapes contain text about transaction signatures, the mint model, public announcement and agreement on transaction history. |
| Order and stability, yellow writing at the top | Aldous Huxley, Brave New World, chapter 10 | Exact phrase occurs in the Director's denunciation of Bernard Marx. This is a strong literary reference, not a cipher alphabet key. |
| Brave new world | Shakespeare, The Tempest, act 5 scene 1; also Huxley's novel | Miranda uses the phrase in the play. Its presence alone does not identify an extraction rule or another symbol alphabet. |
| Gravity Falls symbol family | Gravity Falls: Journal 3, published July 26, 2016 | Chronologically plausible book to inspect. The publisher confirms the book; online reconstructions distinguish several keys. No primary book page was obtained that identifies the terminal unknown mark. |
| Recent Gravity Falls alphabets | The Book of Bill, published July 23, 2024 | Cannot be an original source for a 2020 artwork unless an earlier occurrence of that alphabet is documented. |
| Terminal mark after the right border number caption | Unresolved | No verified book, alphabet identity or value found. It must remain unknown. Resemblance to a rune, alchemical sign or cipher glyph is not sufficient. |

The right border has an existing community Russian plaintext interpretation using geometric substitution symbols. It remains a reading hypothesis. The artwork is treated as an unknown symbol system; a proposed plaintext language and a proposed glyph family are different kinds of labels. The additional marks could be invented extensions, borrowed signs, or another key; the available evidence does not select between these explanations.

The independent community report describes this same terminal glyph as unattested in its tested keys. This is a report of its own measurements, not an author supplied key or an independent proof of origin. Its statement that the glyph must be one of five missing Cyrillic letters assumes a complete, single alphabet and correct plaintexts; those assumptions are not established for every symbol.

Reference pages were searched for Journal 3, the Author key, Bill's key, historical runes, alchemical symbols and Pigpen. Search results do not prove a match. Direct retrieval of the dCode chart pages was blocked with HTTP 403, so no new automatic full alphabet comparison or recovered assignment is claimed.

The initial pass read selected Huxley passages. The later Brave New World comparison now reviews all eighteen chapters of the Huxley.net transcription, with seventeen classified artwork parallels, chapter links and a literal search audit. See Research view → Brave New World comparison and reports/brave-new-world-comparison.md. No complete decipherment is claimed.

## Sources

- https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf
- https://huxleyarchive.org/Fiction/COVERS/Brave%20New%20World.pdf
- https://www.folger.edu/explore/shakespeares-works/the-tempest/read/5/1/
- https://books.disney.com/book/gravity-falls-journal-3/
- https://books.disney.com/book/the-book-of-bill/
- https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U1F700.pdf
- https://www.nist.gov/document/ccawpigpencipherpdf
- https://github.com/rarsn4/blm-0.2btc-analysis/blob/main/REPORT.md

Online key reconstructions used only as research leads:

- https://www.dcode.fr/gravity-falls-journal-3-cipher
- https://www.dcode.fr/gravity-falls-author-cipher
- https://gravityfalls.fandom.com/wiki/List_of_cryptograms/Books

files.text:
# Whitepaper image extraction and comparison

The visible source is section 2, Transactions, on printed page 2 of the [Bitcoin whitepaper](https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf). The image places the final paragraph's beginning inside WELCOME TO THE, earlier paragraphs inside BRAVE NEW WORLD, and its closing continuation along the bottom border.

This is a manual provisional transcription from the supplied image. It is not a certified complete word for word extraction. Lowercase/uppercase forms, punctuation, some letters, and physical line breaks remain uncertain. The artwork runs text along curved letter strokes; wrapping that into ordinary prose necessarily changes its layout. No missing words have been silently restored from the reference.

Each numbered entry corresponds to one title letter. The text below preserves apparent spelling and the explicitly recorded word fragments. It is a reading along the letter strokes, not a facsimile of every physical line. [A?] and [which?] are uncertain readings; square bracket spans remain unreadable.

## Differences from the reference

| Location | Visible artwork | Reference | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BRAVE E | introdue | introduce | Apparent missing c; legible in enlarged crop |
| BRAVE E | No visible words between introdue and cent / ral | a trusted | Apparent omission; initial A before common remains uncertain |
| NEW E | dou / dle- / spent | double-spent | Apparent b to d substitution; split strokes make confidence lower |
| WORLD O | sing | sign | Apparent transposition of the last two letters |
| WORLD D | abcense | absence | Apparent s to c substitution |
| THE H | participans | participants | Apparent missing t; handwritten join is ambiguous |
| Footer | recived | received | Apparent missing e; partly crossed by frame |
| WELCOME TO | No visible citation marker after announced | [1] | Reference citation marker is not visibly reproduced |
| Footer tail | Several words crossed by black frame | See section 2 closing sentence | Not transcribed from reference; remains obscured |

## Reading order and limits

The artwork's displayed order starts with a later part of the whitepaper. To compare source order, read BRAVE NEW WORLD first, then WELCOME TO THE, then the footer. This reordering is an explicit comparison step; it does not alter the saved image transcription.

Word fragments can be joined for searching the reference, but their original splits remain in the letter records. In particular, joining the apparent dou/dle gives doudle, not double. The reference citation marker [1] after announced is not visible in the artwork.

The footer's tail is under the black border. Its expected wording is recoverable from the reference, but that would be reconstruction, not image extraction. The saved transcription therefore retains unreadable spans. The apparent word before they is also marked uncertain rather than asserted to match the reference.

The CSV lists observed differences rather than repeating the complete external whitepaper. Use the linked PDF for an authoritative view of the full original section. The JSON retains the supplied image hash, exact saved strings, uncertainty labels, reading order and explicit word joining operations.

## Every word alignment

[Open the complete word alignment CSV](whitepaper-every-word-alignment.csv). Every matched image token has its source position recorded. Differences are grouped into insertions or replacements; they are flagged for review, not silently corrected. The reference contains 286 tokens under the documented tokenizer; the provisional image reading has 282 after explicit fragment joins. Of those, 270 align as equal after ignoring case. These counts describe this transcription and tokenizer, not measured OCR accuracy or a hidden message. The raw letter records retain spelling, fragment splits and uncertain readings.
